regulator.value: TASE (ISA-supervised exchange) for every member; the Bank of Israel for banks' stability
regulator.notes: Trading on TASE goes only through TASE members: banks, non-bank members (חש"בים) and remote members (BRK-01, BRK-32). TASE supervises members under its rules, which the ISA approves; for banks that supervision covers trading and conduct only, their stability being the Bank of Israel's (BRK-04). The ISA supervises TASE itself (REG-13). A foreign broker reached under a section 49A permit is not ISA-supervised (BRK-06); a pending broker-dealer bill would add an ISA licence (BRK-05, secondary).

source.title: Banking (Service to Customer) (Fees) Rules 2008, consolidated to 5.11.2024, first schedule part 4(א)(1)

trade.notes: No regulatory cap. For banks the rules fix the fee type (a percentage of the trade with a minimum and a maximum, separately for shares and bonds and for makam) but each bank sets the price; a direct-channel fee must be lower than the clerk fee; two weeks' notice of changes. Non-bank members follow the same part structure; their tariff is a ceiling and negotiated prices exist. TASE publishes every member's average fees actually charged, by security type and portfolio band.

source.title: Banking (Service to Customer) (Fees) Rules 2008, consolidated to 5.11.2024, first schedule part 4(א)(5) and notes

custody.notes: No regulatory cap on the rate (banks: a percentage with a maximum per deposit, price set by the bank). Banks may not charge it at all on makam or on money-market fund units (BRK-17, BANK-18); the ban binds banks only, and no rule limits a non-bank member's custody fee on them (BRK-17, BRK-52; BRK open question 11 closed 2026-10-26). Non-bank members name it דמי משמרת or דמי ניהול/טיפול פיקדון ני"ע.

source.title: Banking (Service to Customer) (Fees) Rules 2008, consolidated to 5.11.2024, first schedule part 5 (עמלת חליפין)

fx.notes: No regulatory cap. A bank converts at its rate plus the conversion fee when a foreign security is paid for or sold without enough foreign currency in the account; non-bank members charge a conversion fee or a spread on the rate (מרווח המרה).

source.title: מדריך לחברי הבורסה: החלק הראשון לתקנון (מעודכן עד 1.1.2026), עמוד 23, סעיף 18; עמוד 35, סעיף 29ב, 29ג(2)

fixed_period.notes: No cap in law or in the exchange rules: every member reports its fees to TASE and states them in the client agreement, and no rule makes a published tariff a ceiling (BRK-24). A bank may charge only for services in the Governor's full tariff, or added with the Supervisor's approval (BRK-16, BANK-16). Whether a member charges a monthly account fee, and how much, is its own tariff (BRK-48, BRK-28, on the companies' pages).

source.title: מדריך לחברי הבורסה: החלק הראשון לתקנון (מעודכן עד 1.1.2026), עמוד 23, סעיף 18; עמוד 35, סעיף 29ב, 29ג(2)

distribution_handling.notes: No cap in law or in the exchange rules: every member reports its fees to TASE and states them in the client agreement, and no rule makes a published tariff a ceiling (BRK-24). Whether a member charges on interest, dividend and redemption payments is its own tariff (BRK-48, on the companies' pages).

source.title: Banking (Service to Customer) (Fees) Rules 2008, consolidated to 9.4.2025, first schedule part 4(א)(6) notes, part 5 item 10

transfer_out.notes: Banks only: moving the portfolio to the same client's account at another financial body on closing the account costs at most NIS 10 for the transfer and third-party costs; while the account stays open the price is supervised: at most NIS 5 for the service plus what the bank paid a third party, per the Bank of Israel's fees page (SW-33; BRK OQ12 closed 2026-11-06); the page names no unit, and Discount prints per transfer (SW-52, institution). Non-bank members have no cap found and charge per security (SW-34).

labels: secondary source: an accumulating foreign-domiciled fund is taxed only at sale (TXF-11; TXF OQ1)
institution source: tax when securities move between accounts without a sale (SW-36; SW OQ11)

lawful_exit.text: any TASE trading day (Monday to Friday since 5.1.2026, BRK-29): sell on the exchange, or redeem Israeli ETF and fund units through the member (ETF-04); the proceeds settle through the TASE clearing house. A trade on the exchange settles on the next business day (GOV-24). Foreign funds on TASE and foreign-domiciled funds are sold on an exchange only.

source.title: Income Tax Ordinance, s.88 definition of "מכירה" (includes exchange and redemption); s.101A(a)(12)

switch_is_tax_event.notes: Selling one fund or security to buy another is a sale: tax on any real gain is withheld even if the money never leaves the account (TXS-21). Moving securities in kind to your own account at another member is described by institutions as not a tax event, with the cost basis carried over; no Tax Authority source was read (SW-36, SW OQ11).

eligibility.text: anyone who opens a securities account at a bank that is a TASE member or at a non-bank TASE member (a written custody agreement at a bank); minimums are provider-set (each provider's own terms: BRK-28, on the companies' pages); rules for minors' accounts were not found (BRK OQ17); a foreign broker is reached directly or through a section 49A permit holder (BRK OQ9); trading is on TASE trading days, Monday to Friday since 5.1.2026

protection.text: TASE securities, at a bank or a non-bank member alike, are registered at the clearing house in the member's name as trustee for its clients, in a client sub-account kept apart from the member's own (BRK-58, REG-35), and every member keeps a separate account for each client (BRK-07, BRK-10); a non-bank member must also hold client cash in trust at banks, with a yearly independent audit (REG-16, BRK-08). The Trust Law lets trust assets be reached only for debts on them or arising from the trust (REG-34); that this keeps clients' securities out of a failing member's estate is a reading of these texts, which no law states in words and no court decision read confirms, and a client's claim for a shortfall would be a general debt (a reading of REG-34). Cash in a bank securities account is a deposit, and deposits are not insured (REG-35, REG-04). The clearing house guarantees settlement between members, not a client's balance (REG-15, BRK-58), and no Israeli investor-compensation scheme was found (BRK-58). Still open: who moves a failed member's accounts (REG OQ9, REG OQ10), whether the clearing house's lien reaches the client sub-account (BRK OQ23), whether a non-bank member's client cash is exposed to the bank holding it (REG OQ21), and what happens to foreign securities held through a failing bank (REG OQ23). Abroad: SIPC for a US broker-dealer and the Irish scheme for IB Ireland, as stated by those bodies
